Marissa/Hannah —

Quick triage from infra: we're seeing a clear throughput spiral in us-west-2a concentrated on the fastest low-latency pool that's serving Sunridge (pool-sr-01). Evidence: sudden KV cache churn (TTL eviction spike) + continuous batching backlog causing short-lived OOMs in the runtime shards — that leads to transient 502s when worker threads drop requests.

Immediate actions taken (10:00 PDT):
- Enabled cross-region steering to us-west-2b for 30% of Sunridge traffic (gradual ramp) to shed pressure on pool-sr-01.
- Bumped reserved pool concurrency for Sunridge by adding two warm instances (allowed extra burst capacity).
- Forced model fallback to quantized-compat variant (lower memory pressure) for non-privileged routes.
- Dropped batch size cap from 64 -> 32 for this customer's route to reduce per-request latency variance.

Preliminary impact: P95 improved ~25% on routed traffic; 502s rate dropped but not yet back to baseline. We're continuing to monitor KV cache eviction patterns and will consider aggressive KV cache pinning for their hot prefixes if needed.

We're opening INF-4521 and will attach runtime traces; I'll follow with pinpointed trace IDs.

— David
David Kim
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Quick operations update:

Observed behavior: routing flapping between us-west-2a pools when pool-sr-01 hit sustained GC/eviction pressure; load balancer health checks caused short drain cycles and amplified retries. This is the classic 'throughput spiral' — retries cause higher instantaneous QPS, which triggers more evictions, etc.

Short-term mitigations enacted:
- Stabilized LB health check window (extended failure threshold) to avoid noisy drains.
- Applied a temporary QoS rule to limit retries from our edge for this customer to 1 retry over 2s.
- Initiated an emergency canary rehome to us-west-2c for 15% of traffic to validate behavior before a wider shift.

Needs from leadership / sales:
- Approval to request a priority-pin (customer priority lane) until we complete a durable fix (pin request will affect other customers' failover budgets).
- Approval to offer Sunridge a one-time usage credit for the impacted window if they escalate formally. Suggestion: 20% credit for July 16 incident window.

I'll keep monitoring; logs show recovery on the routed portion but original AZ still noisy.

— Hannah
